relationship: A journey's motion is encoded by distance-time gradient and speed-time area, with the trolley providing the same event in physical and graphical forms.

learnerLoop.action: Edit a journey, run or scrub the trolley, and complete the requested calculation.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Journey timings, graph segments and the trolley position update together.
learnerLoop.evidence: The linked animation, graphs, limits and checked working show rate or accumulated distance.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Revise a segment or use gradient or area to meet the journey constraint.

invariants: Distance-time gradient represents speed for each segment.
safeAdaptations: Vary solvable journey constraints and graph values.
Adjust calculation support while keeping the trolley and graph synchronised.
nonGoals: Interpreting graph shape without relating it to the journey it represents.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

settings.description: Mode, support and optional goal editing.
settings.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

playback.description: Run, pause and inspect time without adding a separate answer quantity.
playback.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

journey-constraints.description: Route distances, required stop, deadline and camera/kinematic limits.
journey-constraints.source: Given by generated or edited goal.
journey-constraints.output: Goal, constraint strip and reference rule expose the relevant limits.

time-controls.description: Arrival and departure are graph coordinates; typed answers are section travel durations, not necessarily absolute times.
time-controls.domain: Seconds, ordered within the journey deadline.
time-controls.source: Drag free points; required duration entries place locked points.
time-controls.output: Two moving speeds and stop duration update from the same graph.

speed-controls.description: Four speed–time ending vertices, controlled by dragging or a per-section acceleration/ending-speed calculation.
speed-controls.domain: Nonnegative speed in m/s; entered acceleration in m/s² or ending speed in m/s according to calcType.
speed-controls.source: Working plan selects which vertices are locked to calculations.
speed-controls.output: Changing a vertex changes adjacent slopes/areas and total distance.

modes.distance-time: Existing core mode uses arrival/departure times, two camera speed limits, a stop interval and fixed journey deadline.
modes.speed-time: Existing extended mode uses four sections, speed/acceleration constraints, total area and final position.
modes.none: Available points/vertices are dragged; slope, time and area evidence is shown.
modes.some: One selected segment is controlled by a required calculation.
modes.all: Both moving distance–time sections or all four speed–time sections require calculations.
modes.persistence: Each mode preserves its own Working level, solved counts and availability. These mode names describe existing code, not newly inferred exam alignment.

dependencies: Changing mode selects that mode’s preserved Working state.
Required inputs control the same graph points that are otherwise dragged; an incorrect entry can still visibly move the point.
Run/pause/time scrub examine the journey; verification also checks the relevant graph/goal constraints and required calculations.
implementation.completion: The local success check opens state.popup when the selected mode’s journey constraints and required calculation results agree; the next journey preserves the selected support plan.
